To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the barriers to organizational learning in chartered surveying are: (a) a lack of understanding of what organizational learning is, and how it can help the firm to achieve its goals; (b) a lack of knowledge of how to implement an organizational learning programme; (c) an inability to identify and prioritize organizational learning objectives; (d) a lack of commitment from the firm's top management to organizational learning; (e) a lack of a clear organizational structure and processes to support organizational learning;

(a) organizational learning can be a source of competitive advantages for organizations, but (b) the chartered surveyors profession has a number of barriers to learning, which are not necessarily bad in themselves, but which (c) have to be made explicit by each organization and worked through to enable the organization to find its way forward.
organizational learning is not a simple process that can be implemented by following a set of instructions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: “What are the barriers to learning within the chartered surveyors’ profession?”
organizational learning in the context of professional work, and with the barriers to organizational learning in this context.
the question “How do we learn to learn?” rather than “Why don’t we learn?”
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there are many barriers to organizational learning in chartered surveying, which have to be addressed individually, and that the process of addressing them will be different for each organization, and will involve a complex mix of organizational learning and organizational development.
organizational learning is not easy, and that it is not easy because it is not easy.
there are many different barriers to learning in organizations, and each needs to be addressed on a case‐by‐case basis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that there are many obstacles to organizational learning, but that these obstacles can be overcome.
organizational learning is a process which needs to be nurtured and supported by the whole organization, not just by a few individuals or a few departments.
the barriers to organizational learning in chartered surveying can be overcome by the profession, but that the profession will need to be more open to change and to new ways of learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the barriers to organizational learning are not necessarily insurmountable, but that they do need to be recognized and addressed by those in charge.
organizational learning is an ongoing, dynamic, complex, and often contradictory process, rather than a straightforward, one‐way street.
, for each organization, the process of organizational learning needs to start with the organization itself, and its particular context and history.
